Operating a vehicle in any other manner demonstrating willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property. Vehicles actively engaged in roadway, building, or utility construction are exempt from the restrictions regarding off-roadway operation when such operation is reasonably necessary for the performance of construction work. #### Lane Splitting / Filtering Lane splitting by a two-wheeled vehicle is permitted when performed safely and within the posted speed limit. A rider passing moving traffic shall generally pass on the left-hand side of the vehicle being overtaken and shall not pass on the right side of a moving vehicle. On a two-lane roadway consisting of one lane in each direction, a rider may pass on the left only when there is no conflicting oncoming traffic. On a highway, filtering between lanes of traffic is permitted. A rider may travel between vehicles provided the rider does not use the highway shoulder, does not exceed the posted speed limit, and maintains a reasonably safe distance from surrounding vehicles. #### U-Turns A driver shall not perform a U-turn: Across a roadway clearly marked with a double solid center line. At an intersection controlled by traffic signals where the maneuver is prohibited. On any roadway clearly marked with a No U-Turn sign or other applicable traffic-control device. The totality of the driver's conduct must demonstrate willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property.

name: Evading an Officer
definition: Any person who, while operating a motor vehicle, willfully flees, fails to yield to, or otherwise attempts to evade a peace officer who is lawfully attempting to detain them. The individual must have reasonably recognized the officer's attempt to initiate a detention and intentionally continued to evade. For the purpose of vehicle enforcement, an attempt to detain is established under the following circumstances: A marked or unmarked law enforcement vehicle, operated by a uniformed or plainclothes peace officer, positions itself behind a moving or stationary vehicle and activates its emergency lights. As required by the Flashing Colored Lights and Sirens Law, the emergency lighting must include at least one forward-facing flashing blue light. A uniformed officer, or a plainclothes officer with reasonably visible law enforcement identification, approaches a stationary or slow-moving vehicle and clearly orders the driver to stop. Verbal commands issued by an officer on foot must be reasonably capable of being heard and understood by the driver. Siren Usage When a driver fails to yield to a forward-facing flashing blue light, the officer should activate their siren to gain the driver's attention. The siren should remain engaged, in accordance with department policy, until the driver reasonably appears to recognize the attempted detention. A driver's failure to immediately yield to emergency lights alone shall not automatically constitute Evading an Officer. Officers must allow a reasonable opportunity for the driver to recognize the attempted detention and safely stop. Evading an Officer may be established when a driver continues failing to yield after both emergency lights and a siren have been activated for a reasonable period, and their conduct demonstrates an intentional refusal to stop. Evading may also be established when a driver clearly acknowledges the attempted detention but deliberately accelerates, flees, or otherwise attempts to avoid law enforcement. Driver Awareness and Intent Officers must consider factors that may reasonably prevent a driver from recognizing an attempted detention, including vehicle soundproofing, traffic noise, vehicle speed, in-car audio, surrounding traffic, and visibility. A driver shall not be charged solely because they failed to immediately recognize emergency lights or a siren when the surrounding circumstances reasonably explain the delay. When an officer positions their vehicle in front of a driver, clearly identifies themselves, or otherwise establishes circumstances demonstrating that the driver recognized the attempted detention, continued intentional flight may constitute Evading an Officer. A driver who deliberately refuses to stop after clearly acknowledging lawful police commands may be charged even if the pursuit does not involve excessive speed or dangerous driving. Termination of Detention Once a driver has been detained, the deactivation of emergency lights or a siren alone does not constitute a release from detention. A driver is considered released only when the law enforcement officer clearly communicates that the detention has concluded.

name: Reckless Evading
definition: Any person who, while committing [3] 60 - Evading an Officer, willfully operates a motor vehicle with extreme disregard for the safety of others, engaging in conduct that creates a substantial and immediate risk of serious bodily injury or death. Reckless Evading requires conduct that demonstrates a significantly greater level of danger than ordinary evasion. The offense shall not be established solely through excessive speed, disregard for traffic control devices, unsafe lane changes, minor collisions, or other common traffic violations occurring during a pursuit. Qualifying Conduct Reckless Evading may be established when the suspect knowingly engages in exceptionally dangerous conduct, including but not limited to: Extreme Wrong-Way Driving: Traveling against the flow of traffic at dangerous speeds while approaching or passing occupied vehicles, creating an immediate risk of a serious collision. Deliberate Endangerment: Intentionally driving toward pedestrians, officers, or occupied vehicles in a manner that creates an immediate danger of serious bodily injury. Repeated Near Collisions: Operating a vehicle in a manner that repeatedly forces other motorists or pedestrians to take emergency evasive action to avoid serious collisions. Dangerous Vehicle Maneuvers: Deliberately using a vehicle in a manner that creates an immediate and substantial risk of serious bodily injury or death to nearby individuals. Serious Collisions: Causing a collision through willfully dangerous driving that results in serious bodily injury or demonstrates a substantial and immediate risk of death. Charging Standard Officers must establish that the suspect's conduct went beyond ordinary evasion and created a substantial and immediate danger to identifiable individuals or occupied vehicles. The following circumstances shall NOT independently establish Reckless Evading: Excessive speed, regardless of the speed reached. Running red lights, stop signs, or other traffic control devices. Unsafe lane changes, improper passing, or ordinary traffic weaving. Driving on sidewalks, shoulders, or opposing lanes without creating a substantial and immediate danger to others. Minor collisions, property damage, or temporary loss of vehicle control without additional qualifying circumstances. The presence of multiple traffic violations alone does not automatically establish Reckless Evading. Officers must evaluate the actual danger created by the suspect's actions rather than relying solely on the number or severity of traffic violations. A collision or injury is not required when the suspect's conduct otherwise establishes a substantial and immediate risk of serious bodily injury or death.

name: Possession of a Controlled Substance
category: National Law [7] Health and Safety Code
definition: A controlled substance is generally a drug or chemical whose manufacture, possession and use is regulated, such as illicitly used drugs or prescription medications that are designated by law. This code categorizes controlled substances into two categories: Prescription Substances and Illicit Substances. Prescription Substances Prescription Substances may only be possessed and/or handled by the following persons: "Medical Employees" including Emergency Medical Technicians, Paramedics, Doctors, Nurses, Pharmacists, Pharmaceutical Technicians, and medically trained police officers\ (\special allowance of Epinephrine, IVS, Morphine, Tranexamic Acid, and Midazolam). Medical Employees may only possess prescription substances for the purpose of performing medical treatment on patients. Medical Employees may not possess prescription substances for the purpose of administering it to themselves or providing it to a non-medical employee without a prescription. "Individuals" including persons with medical prescriptions issued to them by a doctor or nurse for a specific medication. Individuals who possess prescription substances must also possess the prescription itself (typically located on a form or on a prescription bottle/container). List of Prescription Substances Hydromorphone (Dilaudid®), methadone (Dolophine®), meperidine (Demerol®), oxycodone (OxyContin®, Percocet®), and fentanyl (Sublimaze®, Duragesic®), morphine, opium, codeine, hydrocodone, amphetamine (Dexedrine®, Adderall®), methamphetamine (Desoxyn®), methylphenidate (Ritalin®, Concerta®), amobarbital, glutethimide, and pentobarbital, marijuana (cannabis / "pot/weed"), Codeine®, buprenorphine (Suboxone®), benzphetamine (Didrex®), phendimetrazine, ketamine, Depo®-Testosterone, alprazolam (Xanax®), carisoprodol (Soma®), clonazepam (Klonopin®), clorazepate (Tranxene®), diazepam (Valium®), lorazepam (Ativan®), midazolam (Versed®), temazepam (Restoril®), triazolam (Halcion®), Robitussin AC®, ezogabine, bupropion, trazodone (Desyrel), ondansetron (Zofran®), hydroxyzine (Atarax®), Zolpidem (Ambien®), trenbolone, oxymetholone, methandrostenolone, nandrolone, stanozolol, boldenone, and oxandrolone, cocaine (coke/crack), chlorodiazepoxide (Librium®), eszopiclone (Lunesta®), zaleplon (Sonata®), Gamma-hydroxybutyrate or sodium oxybate (Xyrem®), Flunitrazepam (Rohypnol®), Atomoxetine (Strattera®), Tranexamic Acid, Intravenous Solutions (IVS) (0.9% Normal Saline / NS / 0.9NaCl / or NSS ; Dextrose 5% in Water / D5 or D5W / intravenous sugar solution ; Lactated Ringers / LR / Ringers Lactate or RL ; 0.45% Normal Saline / Half Normal Saline / 0.45NaCl / .45NS). Marijuana (Cannabis) is regulated separately under the Cannabis Regulation and Licensing provisions of this Code and is not subject to the prescription requirements below except where expressly provided. Cannabis Regulation and Licensing Section I — Personal Possession Adults twenty-one (21) years of age or older may lawfully possess cannabis for personal use subject to the following limitations: Up to 3 ounces (approximately 85 grams) of cannabis flower; and Up to 24 grams of concentrated cannabis, including oils, vape cartridges, extracts, concentrates, or infused edible products. Possession within these limits by an adult shall not constitute a criminal offense. Persons under twenty-one (21) years of age remain prohibited from possessing cannabis unless authorized under a valid medical prescription. Possession in excess of these limits remains unlawful unless authorized under a state-issued commercial cannabis license. Nothing in this section authorizes the possession of cannabis with the intent to sell, distribute, or otherwise transfer cannabis for compensation without a valid state-issued license. Section II — Home Storage Adults twenty-one (21) years of age or older may store up to five (5) pounds of cannabis within their private residence. Cannabis stored in excess of this limit shall constitute unlawful possession unless possessed pursuant to a commercial cannabis license. Section III — Home Cultivation Adults twenty-one (21) years of age or older may cultivate: Up to six (6) cannabis plants per individual; or No more than twelve (12) cannabis plants per household regardless of the number of occupants. Plants exceeding these limits are unlawful unless cultivated pursuant to a state-issued cultivation license. Section IV — Consumption Cannabis may be consumed: Within a private residence; In any public location where cigarette smoking is otherwise lawfully permitted. Cannabis consumption remains prohibited: Inside any motor vehicle; On school property; On federal property; In any location where smoking or public drug consumption is otherwise prohibited by law. Section V — Licensed Cannabis Businesses The State of San Andreas shall establish a licensing system authorizing qualified persons or entities to operate cannabis businesses. Licenses may include: Retail Cannabis Dispensaries Cannabis Cultivation Facilities Cannabis Processing Facilities Cannabis Distribution Operations Licensed businesses shall: Obtain and maintain a valid state operating license. Comply with all applicable health and safety regulations. Submit to inspections by authorized state agencies. Maintain accurate inventory and sales records. Remit all required licensing fees and taxes. Operating any cannabis business without the required state license remains unlawful. Section VI — Commercial Regulation The State shall establish regulations governing: Packaging and labeling; Product testing; Quality assurance standards; Inventory and sales tracking; Licensing requirements; Tax collection. Revenue generated through licensing fees and cannabis taxation may be allocated to public safety, emergency services, transportation infrastructure, healthcare, education, and community development. Illicit Substances Illicit Substances may not be possessed by any person. List of Illicit Substances Heroin, lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD), peyote (Mescaline), Quaaludes (methaqualone), methylenedioxymethamphetamine ("Ecstasy"), PCP/Angel Dust (phencyclidine), psilocybin, salvia, ayahuasca, Synthetic Cannabinoids (K2/Spice), Synthetic Cathinones (Bath Salts/Flakka), Psilocybin (Magic Mushrooms/Shrooms)

definition: Controlled Substances It shall be unlawful, and therefore a violation of this code, to manufacture any Illicit Substance as defined by [7] 6 - Possession of a Controlled Substance. It shall be unlawful, and therefore a violation of this code, to manufacture any Prescription Substance as defined by [7] 6 - Possession of a Controlled Substance without: A valid operating permit; A license authorizing production or manufacturing; A physical facility security system; Facility employment records; Commercial operating liability insurance; Self-administered quality control procedures and inspection reports; and A list of substances or products to be manufactured or repackaged. Cannabis Notwithstanding the provisions above, cannabis shall be regulated under the Cannabis Regulation and Licensing provisions of [7] 6 - Possession of a Controlled Substance. The following activities shall be lawful when conducted in compliance with that code: Personal cultivation by adults twenty-one (21) years of age or older, subject to statutory plant limits. Cultivation by holders of a valid State Cannabis Cultivation License. Processing or manufacturing of cannabis products by holders of a valid State Cannabis Processing License. Distribution or transportation of cannabis by holders of a valid State Cannabis Distribution License. Retail sale of cannabis by holders of a valid State Cannabis Retail License. It shall remain unlawful to manufacture, cultivate, process, distribute, or package cannabis outside the authority granted by a valid state license or beyond the personal cultivation limits established by law. Alcohol It shall be unlawful, and therefore a violation of this code, to manufacture any Alcoholic Beverage, defined as any beverage or liquid containing more than one percent (1%) alcohol by volume, without: A valid operating permit; A manufacturing license; A physical facility security system; Facility employment records; Commercial operating liability insurance; Self-administered quality control procedures and inspection reports; and A list of substances or products to be manufactured or repackaged. Tobacco It shall be unlawful, and therefore a violation of this code, to manufacture any Tobacco Product without: A valid operating permit; A manufacturing license; A physical facility security system; Facility employment records; Commercial operating liability insurance; Self-administered quality control procedures and inspection reports; and A list of substances or products to be manufactured or repackaged. For the purposes of this code, a Tobacco Product includes cigarettes, cigars, dissolvable tablets, skin patches, hookah shisha, dip, snuff, snus, chewing tobacco, pipe tobacco, packaged rollable tobacco, vape products, electronic cigarettes, hookah pens, and other electronic nicotine delivery systems. The cultivation of raw tobacco plants and the operation of tobacco farms are not regulated under this section. Transport It shall be unlawful, and therefore a violation of this code, to knowingly transport any Controlled Substance, Alcohol, or Tobacco Product that was illegally produced under this code. This provision shall not apply to: Persons lawfully transporting cannabis in compliance with the Cannabis Regulation and Licensing provisions of [7] 6 - Possession of a Controlled Substance; Licensed cannabis distributors transporting cannabis within the scope of their state-issued license; or Individuals transporting cannabis lawfully possessed for personal use within the statutory possession limits. Sale It shall be unlawful, and therefore a violation of this code, to knowingly sell any Controlled Substance, Alcohol, or Tobacco Product that was illegally produced or to sell such products without the licenses required by law. For cannabis: Licensed cannabis retailers may lawfully sell cannabis products in accordance with their state-issued license. Any sale, barter, exchange for value, or commercial distribution of cannabis by an unlicensed person or entity remains unlawful regardless of the quantity involved. Inspections Facilities and entities operating to manufacture, cultivate, process, distribute, or sell controlled substances, cannabis, alcohol, or tobacco products shall be subject to compliance inspections, with or without prior notice, by authorized governmental agencies. Seizure Authority Where there is reasonable suspicion that a controlled substance, cannabis product, alcohol, or tobacco product has been manufactured, cultivated, processed, transported, or sold in violation of this code, the property may be seized even if no individual is ultimately charged with an offense. Facilities and entities operating to produce or sell controlled substances, alcohol, or tobacco products shall be subject to facility and operating inspections for compliance with or without notice. Note that the raw Tobacco plant, or the farm in which they might be produced, is not included within this code. If a given substance is reasonably suspected of being illegally manufactured, the item may be seized even if no person is charged with an offence (such as when they were unaware of the illegality of the substance).
